title: How Voice AI Handles Shopify and Recharge Subscription Calls With Gorgias Handoffs
summary: Learn how voice AI handles Shopify and Recharge support calls, verifies callers, and routes complex cases to human agents using Gorgias.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- This guide covers a phone-first workflow for subscription brands that use Shopify for orders, Recharge for subscriptions, and Gorgias for human support.
- SigmaMind AI describes[Shopify customer and order lookups](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) and[Recharge subscription lookups](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) . Confirm the available fields and live-call behavior in your configuration.
- Test phone transfer and Gorgias ticket write-back separately. Confirm which Recharge actions the agent can perform before enabling subscription changes.
- The workflow suits brands with substantial inbound phone volume. A chat-first brand with few calls may have little reason to build it.


## Who this workflow is for


Brands with substantial inbound phone volume can use Shopify order and Recharge subscription lookups to answer supported questions, then transfer unresolved calls to a person. A separate, tested process can pass approved call context into Gorgias.


The guide assumes you already use Gorgias for support tickets and have a phone system that can route calls to human agents. SigmaMind AI is an option if you want voice AI alongside your existing phone system, but you must establish how call context reaches Gorgias. If most customers contact you through chat and phone calls are rare, the integration work may outweigh the value of automating those calls.


## The three systems and what each one is responsible for


An authorized Shopify lookup can supply order and fulfillment information, such as a recorded shipment status. SigmaMind AI[describes its Shopify connector](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) as fetching customer profiles, order status, and basic fulfillment details. Its published description does not document order-changing actions. Shopify’s[Admin GraphQL API](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql) uses access tokens with requested scopes. Limit the connection’s access to the data needed for order lookups.


An authorized Recharge lookup can supply the subscription details and scheduled dates available to the configured connection. SigmaMind AI[describes its Recharge connector](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) as retrieving active subscriptions and plan details, and says agents can modify subscriptions. Before enabling a pause or date change, you need to confirm the connector’s permissions and the caller-confirmation steps. Check the applicable[Recharge API permissions](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/) and whether your configured connection supports separate read and write access. If it does, use read-only access for routine lookups. Grant write access for a specific action only after confirming that the connection supports it and that caller verification and confirmation work.


Gorgias can hold the support ticket and approved lookup context for a human agent, but the phone transfer and the ticket update are separate steps. The[SigmaMind AI listing on Gorgias’s app marketplace](https://www.gorgias.com/apps/sigma-ai) describes ticket automation and chat-oriented modes, not a native phone handoff or call-summary sync. SigmaMind AI[lists Gorgias in its app library](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/) , but the available documentation does not establish a ready-made ticket or call-summary sync for this workflow. You need to configure and test that context transfer separately from the phone transfer.


The cited materials do not document a ready-made three-way workflow for Shopify, Recharge, and Gorgias. Confirm how your configured integrations, APIs, or middleware will match records and pass call context between them.


## Step-by-step: how a call moves through the system


1. SigmaMind AI answers the call and uses a phone number or email address to find a possible customer record. If several records match, configure the agent to request another identifier, such as an order number, or transfer the call. Before disclosing account details, the agent must apply your configured identity-verification check. An order number or record match alone does not prove that the caller owns the account.
2. The agent retrieves the information needed for the question. SigmaMind AI documents a[Shopify connection](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) that fetches orders and fulfillment details, and a[Recharge connection](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) that fetches active subscriptions and plan details. Configure the call flow to request current records, and confirm which fields each connection returns during a live call.
3. The agent answers questions that the retrieved records support. For example, it can give an order status when Shopify returns one or tell a caller which subscription plan Recharge shows. A request to pause a subscription needs a separate decision. Recharge offers write actions, but you must confirm the enabled action, its permissions, and the caller-confirmation step before letting the agent make a change.
4. The agent transfers calls it cannot safely resolve. Conflicting records, failed lookups, billing disputes, refund requests, and payment-method changes should not produce a guessed answer or an assumed account action. The call flow should tell the caller that a human agent will take over.
5. Use a tested transfer method to give the receiving agent the reason for transfer and any approved lookup results. If that method passes context, include the verified customer identifier, relevant order or subscription, caller request, and any lookup failure. If the transfer fails or no one is available, tell the caller and use your tested callback or follow-up process. Test Gorgias write-back separately. Although SigmaMind AI[lists Gorgias as an integration](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/) , the cited materials do not establish automatic ticket creation or call-summary sync for this workflow.


## Caller identification and data permissions


A phone or email match should locate a customer record, not authorize access to it. SigmaMind AI says its[Shopify integration](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) can identify customers by phone or email and retrieve order information. Its[Recharge integration](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) describes customer and subscription lookups. Your implementation must confirm how it links the two records and handles missing or duplicate matches. A caller may know someone else’s email or call from a spoofed number, so a match alone should not release account details.


Give the voice agent only the permissions it needs to answer approved questions. Shopify requires apps to request[specific access scopes](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql) . Recharge separates[read permissions for customers, orders, and subscriptions](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/) from write permissions for actions such as changing a subscription or payment method. Use scoped, read-only credentials for lookups, and reserve write access for actions you have explicitly configured and approved.


The available SigmaMind AI integration descriptions do not define a verification threshold for billing changes. Before enabling any sensitive action, define a verification check independent of the phone or email match, require the caller to confirm the exact proposed change, and specify when a human must take over. Test the check against duplicate records and callers who know someone else’s email or order number. If the agent cannot verify the caller under your policy, it should withhold account details and transfer the call.


## Example call scenarios


An order-status call can end with the voice agent when the Shopify lookup returns current fulfillment details. For example, a caller asks, “Where is order 1042?” If the caller passes the configured check and Shopify returns current shipment details, the agent could relay the returned status and tracking information. SigmaMind AI[documents order and fulfillment lookups](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) . If the lookup returns no tracking details, the agent should say so rather than invent an update. For a fuller order-status workflow, see the[Shopify order-status guide](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/voice-ai-shopify-order-status-returns) .


A subscription skip request depends on which Recharge actions the implementation permits. A caller asks, “Can I skip next month’s delivery?” The agent checks the subscription. It can discuss the next scheduled charge only if the configured lookup returns that field. If you have verified and enabled the specific skip action, the agent can confirm the requested date before making the change. Otherwise, it can explain the schedule and transfer the request. SigmaMind AI[describes subscription changes](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) , but its published post does not specify the write permissions or confirmation steps.


A failed-payment question can require a human even when the agent can find the account. A caller says, “Why did you charge me again after my payment failed in January?” The agent should not decide a dispute from a subscription lookup alone. Your implementation must confirm which charge history it can retrieve and transfer questions that require investigation, refunds, or payment-method changes with the caller’s question and approved account context.


An account restriction or failed lookup should stop an automated subscription change. A caller says, “My account is locked, but I need to change my subscription today.” If a separately configured account-status check identifies a restriction, or a Shopify lookup returns an access error, the agent should avoid guessing at the cause and transfer the request to a human. An API error alone does not establish a fraud flag or explain why an account is locked. Sending a summary into Gorgias requires a separately configured and tested handoff.


## Escalation criteria and the handoff to Gorgias


Transfer a call when the agent cannot resolve it through permitted lookups or the caller requests an action outside its approved scope. Send billing disputes that require charge investigation, refund requests, and payment-method changes to a human agent. An account flagged for fraud, a locked account, a failed customer match, or a Shopify or Recharge API error should also stop automated handling. For a failed payment, the agent can relay a status it can retrieve, but a human should handle questions that require a billing decision.


SigmaMind AI’s[warm-transfer article](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/warm-transfer) describes preparing a summary and passing context variables to a receiving agent. Confirm which of those steps your phone-system configuration supports before using them in this workflow. For a subscription pause request, those details could include the matched customer record, the subscription in question, and why the agent could not complete the request. If your phone-transfer configuration supports a private whisper, it can give the human agent that context while the caller remains on the line. Keep payment credentials out of the summary.


A voice transfer does not automatically create a Gorgias ticket or place the summary in one. If you need that context in Gorgias, configure and test middleware or an API workflow that matches the call to the right customer and writes the approved details. The available documentation does not establish a pre-built SigmaMind AI and Gorgias sync or confirm that a ticket will appear before the agent answers. Until you validate ticket timing, use a tested method to brief the receiving agent during the live handoff and follow your existing ticket process.


## Operational safeguards for billing and account actions


Before enabling a subscription change, verify that the configured Recharge connection supports the specific action and grant only the required[Recharge API permissions](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/) . Keep[Shopify access scopes](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql) limited to the order data the agent needs. Define how the caller proves account ownership, confirms the requested change, and reaches a human when approval is required. A phone or email match alone does not authorize a billing change.


Transfer calls when an API cannot provide a reliable answer. A Shopify or Recharge lookup may fail because access is denied, the service is unavailable, or the API limits requests. In those cases, pass the caller’s question and the error category to a human agent rather than guessing or reading an API error aloud.


Route billing questions to a human when the available charge history does not support an answer. Confirm the history returned by your Recharge configuration before deciding which questions the agent may handle. Recharge documents refund and payment-related API actions, but that does not establish that SigmaMind AI enables them in this voice workflow. Keep refunds and payment-method changes with a human unless you have confirmed the integration, permissions, and caller-verification controls.


## Implementation checklist


- \[ \] Confirm that SigmaMind AI can match a caller to the correct Shopify customer and Recharge subscription. Test duplicate phone numbers, mismatched email addresses, and records that appear in only one system.
- \[ \] Set a verification threshold before the agent reads account details. Require a stronger check for sensitive actions, and document when the agent must transfer instead.
- \[ \] Start with read-only access for order and subscription lookups. Confirm which Recharge write actions are enabled in your configuration, which require API or middleware work, and which remain human-only.
- \[ \] Test the phone transfer and Gorgias write-back independently. Confirm what context the receiving agent hears or sees during the call, then verify whether your configured ticket workflow creates a ticket, updates an existing one, or does neither.
- \[ \] Test failed lookups, denied access, locked accounts, and rate-limit responses. Make sure the agent stops the affected action and transfers the caller rather than guessing or reading an API error aloud.
- \[ \] Test live lookup latency at expected call volume. Check applicable[Shopify Admin GraphQL API limits](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql) and[Recharge API documentation](https://developer.rechargepayments.com/) for your configuration, and confirm that the agent handles slow, limited, or unavailable responses during a call.
- \[ \] Review SigmaMind AI’s[Shopify integration post](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-shopify) and[Recharge integration post](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/sigmamind-recharge) for the underlying connector details, then validate the configured actions in your own environment.


## Deciding whether to build this workflow


Estimate how many calls need a Shopify order lookup, a Recharge subscription lookup, or both before building the handoff. For example, a question about the next box may require both fulfillment and renewal information. If either lookup fails, the agent should transfer the call rather than guess.


Pilot SigmaMind AI with a small set of frequent order and subscription calls if your brand has substantial phone volume. Test caller verification, the Shopify and Recharge fields returned during live calls, permitted actions, failed lookups, and the context a human actually receives. Test Gorgias ticket write-back separately before making it part of the handoff. Start with read-only calls, review where verification or lookups fail, and add a subscription action only after its permissions and confirmation flow pass testing. You can[sign up to test a SigmaMind AI pilot](https://dashboard.sigmamind.ai/p/signup) before routing live calls. If phone calls are rare, prioritize the support channel customers already use.
